messages.author: 3c8299ac8234f5d2
messages.subject: AIC in MRDS
parts:
Dear list,

I have a question regarding model selection using the MRDS engine.

=46rom my reading of the literature, I understand that point independence=
(PI) models often tend to outperform, and be selected against, their ful=
l independence (FI) equivalent. This was the case for example in the golf=
tee survey described in the advanced book, or in a survey of crabeater s=
eals undertaken by Borchers et al. (2006) - Accommodating unmodeled heter=
ogeneity in double-observer distance sampling surveys, Biometrics 62(2):3=
72-8.

I have been analysing aerial survey data for bottlenose dolphins using MR=
DS, and, contrary to the above scenario, all my FI models have a lower AI=
C value than their correspond PI form.

In a previous post to the list (dated 8th March 2010), Jeff Laake wrote t=
hat he rarely saw real examples in which PI was not favored over FI. I ta=
ke from this that, although unusual, this situation can still occur (and =
is not necessarily the sign of an analysis gone wrong?).=20

I have been scratching my head to find a plausible explanation for these =
results, and the only reasoning I could come up with is that (1) I have a=
very narrow survey strip (w=3D450 m), so there likely isn't much room fo=
r unmodelled heterogeneity away from the trackline, especially once covar=
iates are added into the models, and (2) PI models are effectively more c=
otsly to fit than FI models on small datasets like mine (n =3D 36 sightin=
gs) (as they require the estimation of more parameters - some for the CDS=
component, and some for the MRDS component) ...?

Has anyone else obtained lower AIC scores in FI models compared to PI mod=
els?
I would appreciate your thoughts/comments on the topic.

Thanks in advance -- Phil

messages.author: 3c8299ac8234f5d2
messages.subject: Re: AIC in MRDS
parts:
Dear all,

Below are the responses I received. Many warm thanks to Jeff and Brett fo=
r their prompt feedback.

Brett Collier ----

I suspect that Jeff will respond to you in the near term as he is the exp=
ert on this, but I think that your diagnosis, based off of your email, if=
fairly accurate in that you have a fairly narrow strip so perhaps the di=
stance heterogeneity does not come into play. We had the same issue with=
some avian point count surveys where their was no difference between FI =
and PI (see link below), which was probably a result of 1) not enough dis=
tance bins and 2) fairly high detectability in the 2 bins when the birds =
call.

http://irnr.tamu.edu/bret/BretWebSiteDocs/CollierLF2013.pdf

For what its worth, it 'can' happen, but when it does it is typically bec=
ause we constrained the system in such a way that the distance effects ar=
e not yet being observed, such as in the 2 bin bird point count case wher=
e I saw the same thing.

Jeff Laake -----

FI was the best model in Buckland et al. (2010) in Biometrics for the min=
ke whale data. Your reasoning is sound and while PI is the most common o=
utcome it is not the only possible outcome.

Cheers -- Phil
